extracted.intended_audience: regulators, policy-makers, stakeholder engagement practitioners, and public comment writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and evaluating public consultation inputs and regulatory policy design in line with OECD best practice principles. Focuses on what makes consultation and comments effective and how governments should conduct rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: governments follow good rulemaking at every stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Better regulation requires that governments consistently follow principles of good rulemaking at every stage of the policy cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply consistent good-practice principles across problem identification, option development, impact assessment, implementation, and review to improve regulatory outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focusing on issues that matter to people
rubrics_metrics.description: Focusing on issues that matter to people
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise regulatory effort on problems that have clear, significant impacts on citizens and businesses; ensure the problem is well-defined from users' perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listening to people's ideas for solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Listening to their ideas for solutions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage stakeholders early and meaningfully to surface practical solutions and user experience insights that can improve regulatory design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using evidence to compare different options
rubrics_metrics.description: Using evidence to compare different options
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base option appraisal on empirical evidence and comparative analysis (costs, benefits, risks, and trade-offs) rather than intuition or precedent alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting the details of rules right to ensure they improve outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting the details of rules right to ensure they improve outcomes for people
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to implementation details, clarity, and enforceability so that regulations achieve intended results without unintended burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance of regulators
rubrics_metrics.description: The governance of regulators
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure appropriate institutional arrangements, accountability and oversight for regulatory bodies to promote coherent, high-quality rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and inspections (and toolkit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforcement and inspections, and its toolkit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design enforcement approaches and inspection regimes that are proportionate, risk-based, and supported by clear guidance and practical tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory impact assessment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess expected costs, benefits and distributional impacts of regulatory proposals systematically to inform decision-making and choose the least burdensome effective option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex post reviews of regulatory stock
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex post reviews of regulatory stock
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly review existing regulations to check whether they remain necessary, effective and efficient, and to identify opportunities for repeal or simplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-stop shops for citizens and business
rubrics_metrics.description: One-stop shops for citizens and business
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide consolidated, user-friendly access points for information and services to reduce compliance costs and improve service delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: International regulatory cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: International regulatory cooperation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with other jurisdictions where cross-border effects exist to reduce fragmentation, promote consistency and address transnational issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish transparent, inclusive processes for stakeholder input throughout the policy cycle to improve legitimacy and practical quality of regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation timeliness and stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Are timely and at the right stage of policy development
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold consultations early enough to influence options and late enough to provide meaningful input on feasible designs; avoid token or post-hoc consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple consultation channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple channels (online, in-person, targeted)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine broad public calls with targeted outreach and in-person engagement to reach diverse stakeholder groups and obtain detailed technical input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of accessible documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide accessible documentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish clear, concise background materials, impact assessments and question prompts in accessible formats and languages to enable informed responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcoming diverse and underrepresented perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Welcome diverse perspectives, including from underrepresented groups
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively seek participation from groups that are typically underrepresented and consider barriers to engagement (timing, format, accessibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis and public response to consultation input
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthesize and respond publicly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarise consultation responses publicly and explain how stakeholder input influenced decisions, noting where views were not taken up and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrating impact of consultation on policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate impact on policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show tangible examples of how consultation changed policy design, including amendments, alternatives adopted, or rationale for retaining proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite evidence (preferably independent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite evidence (preferably independent)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support submissions with empirical data, independent studies, impact estimates or concrete examples rather than assertions or anecdote alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the regulator's stated objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with the regulator's stated objectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame comments in relation to the policy goals the regulator has set, explaining how proposed changes support, refine, or better achieve those objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose specific, workable alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose specific, workable alternatives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer concrete drafting suggestions, feasible implementation options, or measurable performance-based approaches rather than vague objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address proportionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Address proportionality (regulatory impact vs. problem scale)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that recommended measures are proportionate to the size and nature of the problem, considering costs, benefits and compliance burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider international consistency where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider international consistency where relevant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note alignment or divergence with international/regional standards and assess cross-border implications to reduce unnecessary trade or compliance frictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge cross-border or international cooperation dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge cross-border or international cooperation dimensions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight opportunities and constraints for cooperation with other jurisdictions and how coordinated approaches could improve outcomes.
